$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1, which is the point of the file living here rather than being generated from the return type.
$janet.$comment.contractField: The envelope stamps 'contract' and the gate cross-checks it against the number above, so code and schema cannot drift apart in either direction.
$janet.$comment.countsNeverNames: There is deliberately no field that could carry a blob name or an entity. A probe can be pointed at an account holding someone else's data without copying any of it into a transcript; adding such a field is a change of purpose, not of format.
$janet.$comment.everyKey: Every key is always present; a value that does not apply is null rather than absent.

contract.description: Bumped only by a format change. An engine change that moves this number is a mistake in one direction; a format change that does not is a mistake in the other.

account.description: The storage account name, as the caller passed it.

subscription.description: The subscription the account was looked up in, and how that was decided.

caller.description: Whose access was tested: the identity in the storage token's own claims, read and not validated. The answer to 'access for whom'.

objectId.description: The token's oid claim: the object id a data role must be granted to. Null when the token could not be read as a JWT or carried no oid.

name.description: The token's upn, else unique_name, else appid (for a service principal). Null when none was present or the token could not be read.

settings.description: The account as the management plane describes it: the settings that decide who can reach the data. Each string is verbatim from ARM, and null means ARM did not report it.

resourceGroup.description: The resource group, read out of the id.

provisioningState.description: ARM's provisioningState for the account; Succeeded for one that is usable.

statusOfPrimary.description: Whether the primary location is available or unavailable.

allowSharedKeyAccess.description: False when account keys and SAS signed with them are refused, so only Entra tokens work. Null means unset, which Azure treats as ALLOWED.

publicNetworkAccess.description: Enabled, Disabled or SecuredByPerimeter. Null means unset, which Azure treats as Enabled.

networkDefaultAction.description: The firewall's answer to a caller no rule matches: Allow or Deny. With Deny, a caller outside ipRules and virtualNetworkRules gets forbidden with AuthorizationFailure.

networkBypass.description: Which traffic skips the firewall, e.g. AzureServices, Logging, Metrics, None.

ipRules.description: How many IP firewall rules there are. Counted, not listed.

virtualNetworkRules.description: How many virtual-network rules there are.

privateEndpoints.description: How many private endpoint connections there are. Non-zero with public access off makes 'unreachable' the expected answer from outside that network.

minimumTlsVersion.description: The lowest TLS version accepted, e.g. TLS1_2.

blobEndpoint.description: The blob service URL the probe used: ARM's primary endpoint, or https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/ when ARM gave none.

tableEndpoint.description: The table service URL the probe used, decided the same way.

summary.description: How many targets ended in each status, every status listed even at zero.

forbidden.description: Targets that refused the caller; each one's errorCode says whether it was a missing role or a network rule.

unreachable.description: Targets where no HTTP answer came back at all.

error.description: Targets that answered with anything else.

targets.description: Each container, then each table, actually read over the data plane with an Entra token. The ones the caller named, or every one the management plane lists, sorted by name.

service.description: Which data-plane service: 'blob' for a container, 'table' for a table.

name.description: The container or table name. Never a blob's name or an entity's key: those are not reported anywhere.

status.description: Can the caller read it? 'ok': yes, and itemsSeen says how much it saw. 'forbidden': HTTP 403 -- with errorCode AuthorizationPermissionMismatch the caller lacks a data role (grant one); with AuthorizationFailure a network rule usually refused them. 'notFound': HTTP 404. 'unreachable': no HTTP answer at all -- DNS, TCP or TLS failed, as when a private endpoint has no route from here or a firewall drops silently. 'error': any other answer, including a success whose body did not parse.

httpStatus.description: The HTTP status the service answered with. Null exactly when status is 'unreachable'.

errorCode.description: The service's own error code (x-ms-error-code, the XML Code element, or the table service's odata.error code), or 'HTTP nnn' when it gave none. Null when there is no error, and for 'unreachable'.

message.description: The service's message, first line only (the rest is a request id and a time); for 'unreachable', the network failure's own message; for an unparseable success, what failed to parse. Null when there is nothing to say.

itemsSeen.description: How many blobs or entities the probe read, at most 5. A count only. Null unless status is 'ok'.

more.description: Whether the service said there was more than it returned. Null unless status is 'ok'.

name.description: The subscription's display name when it was read from the Azure CLI profile. Null when the caller passed an id, which is used as given without a lookup.

source.description: How it was decided. 'explicit': the caller named it, by id or by name. 'az default': the Azure CLI profile's default subscription. 'scope': read out of an ARM id the caller passed.
